FEASIBILITY FINDINGS
Melee's project configuration originally produced a static library, but the work
now has a Windows x86 native proof executable linked against the pinned Aurora
runtime. This does not make it a finished port. Pointer-width/ABI compatibility,
asset loading and relocation, arenas, audio, frame pacing, renderer fidelity,
real input, supported options, networking and packaging each retain separate
tests/gates. D3D12 may be preferred where it proves more stable/faster, with
Vulkan retained for compatibility and capability-checked renderer selection.

SEPARATE LAUNCH TARGETS (user requirement, 2026-10-05)
Bundle two separate launch targets in the desktop package, with matching source:
1. Native Windows game executable: local single-player modes and main-menu
   four-player P2P multiplayer hosting/joining and lobby support.
2. Separate browser-host launcher/build: configurable host IP/address and port,
   producing a join URL that clients open in their browsers. Serve a separately
   compiled browser-compatible game runtime with rendering, input, audio and
   networking, plus assets the host is authorized to distribute. Show each
   client's asset-download progress in the lobby; verify integrity and readiness
   before starting play. A webpage or desktop video stream is not browser play.
Validate browser compilation, transport and cross-client gameplay feasibility
before claiming support. These targets remain roadmap requirements, not delivered
playable builds. Preserve the native runtime acceptance gate above.

INTEGRATION FINDINGS
src/sysdolphin/baselib/archive.c copies big-endian headers directly and rejects
byte-order mismatch; relocation adds pointers through u32. 32-bit pointers alone
do not solve endian conversion. Typed archive conversion is required, not merely
header byte swapping (payload structures include scalars, floats and pointers).
Aurora provides ARQPostRequest in lib/dolphin/AR.cpp, but searches found AXInit,
AXAcquireVoice and AIInit declarations only, with no implementations under lib.
Audio compatibility therefore remains a separate implementation requirement.

2026-10-05: User roadmap clarification - two separate bundled launch/build targets.
1. Native Windows game executable: run locally with single-player modes and main-menu four-player P2P lobby hosting/joining and multiplayer support.
2. Separate browser host launcher/build: serve a browser-compatible game runtime at a configurable host IP address and port (a joinable URL). Guests open that URL in their own browsers, download assets the host is authorized to distribute, and play in the browser. Show each client's asset-download progress in the lobby before readiness/start.
The browser target requires its own compatible compiled runtime, renderer, input, audio and networking; serving a page or launching the desktop executable does not satisfy browser gameplay. Network reachability and browser security requirements must be resolved for the chosen deployment. Native and browser builds must keep compatible gameplay and matching content/mod identities where cross-platform lobbies are supported; cross-platform interoperability needs separate verification.
Bundle both targets with synchronized source, build scripts, dependency versions/notices, rebuild/mod installation instructions and clear launch instructions. Keep the native playable milestone first; browser play and host-to-client asset transfer remain later milestones. Technical asset transfer does not grant redistribution rights. Preserve the original disc and existing saves. Neither launcher alone is a playable port, and both targets remain roadmap work.

2026-10-05 USER ROADMAP REQUIREMENT: Two separate launchers/build targets bundled in the desktop package.
1. Local Windows game executable: runs native single-player locally and provides main-menu hosting/joining of four-player P2P multiplayer lobbies.
2. Separate browser-host executable/build: serves the browser game build, opens the host's browser, and exposes a configurable IP/hostname and port join URL. Joining users download authorized assets and execute the game in their own browsers. Lobby shows each client's asset download progress, integrity/compatibility checks, and readiness before play.
The browser target requires a real browser-compatible game runtime, graphics, input, audio and networking implementation. A webpage launcher or desktop video stream does not fulfill browser play. Network URL exposure, secure browser context and connectivity setup must be validated during this later milestone. Asset transfer supports only content the host is authorized to distribute; technical transfer capability does not grant redistribution rights for original assets.
Both targets must include synchronized modifiable source, build scripts, pinned dependency versions/notices, and rebuild/mod installation instructions in <PRIVATE_INSTALL>. Native playability remains the earlier milestone; neither launcher is currently delivered as playable.

2026-10-06 USER MULTIPLAYER MENU DECISION (supersedes earlier menu wording):
Add main-menu button Online. Its submenu has exactly four entries: Host Game, Join Game, LAN Game, Download Play.
Host Game and Join Game use peer-to-peer networking and support the requested four-player lobbies. LAN Game uses local-area-network hosting/joining without requiring an Internet matchmaking service.
Download Play gracefully closes the current native game and hands off to the separately bundled browser-host launcher/build. Start and validate the host service/browser runtime before completing the handoff so a failed launch can be reported coherently. Relaunch genuine game execution in the host's browser and show the host a shareable join URL. Clients join in their browsers with no assets preinstalled; automatically transfer assets the host is authorized to distribute and display each client's download progress in the lobby. Clients still receive the required assets; this is not a claim that original content can be played with no asset data. Preserve separate native single-player/P2P executable and browser-host executable, synchronized modifiable source, and rebuild/mod instructions. LAN URL reachability and public Internet reachability need separate validation; an IP URL alone does not establish access through NAT. Original asset redistribution authorization remains distinct from technical feasibility.
Status: agreed roadmap, implementation/acceptance pending. Whole-project engineering estimate remains approximately21%.

2026-10-06 USER ROADMAP - ONLINE MENU AND DOWNLOAD PLAY
Main menu includes a button titled Online. Its submenu has exactly four options:
Host Game - host a four-player peer-to-peer lobby.
Join Game - join a peer-to-peer lobby.
LAN Game - multiplayer on the local area network.
Download Play - hand off from the native game to the separately bundled browser-host build. Validate that the browser host can start before closing the current native game; relaunch the host's game in a browser and display a shareable host URL. Clients open that URL in their browsers without preinstalled game assets; the host transfers assets it is authorized to distribute automatically. Show each client's asset download progress in the lobby before play. Distinguish LAN-reachable URLs from Internet-reachable hosting and test connectivity. This is true browser execution, not merely video streaming. No claim of implemented or playable Download Play yet.
Acceptance requires all four menu routes, four-player P2P hosting/joining, LAN play, reliable native-to-browser handoff, host browser play, client asset download/progress and browser multiplayer. Existing graphics, audio, native mods, no-save and synchronized-source packaging requirements remain in scope. Estimated overall project completion remains approximately 21%; this roadmap clarification does not increase completion.

AUDIO OUTPUT PATH FEASIBILITY (2026-10-14)
Source inspection confirms the current native AX backend opens SDL playback from signed 16-bit, two-channel, 32 kHz PCM (aurora/lib/dolphin/AX.cpp: SDL_AudioSpec spec{SDL_AUDIO_S16,2,32000}); aurora_ax_render_frames and the AI streaming gain API are stereo buffers. The graphics/settings page does not yet have a native audio-output page. So the requested Stereo/5.1 choice is feasible only after adding an explicit six-channel output mixer/route, querying the selected SDL device's channel capability, and falling back to stereo when 5.1 is unavailable; merely changing the SDL device format could silently misroute game audio. Verification still required on a real 5.1-capable device, stereo fallback, and clean muted operation. No audio source or settings behavior changed in this inspection. The current Release native library target is up to date (`cmake --build work/build-melee-win32-release --target melee --parallel 4` reported no work); library SHA-256 54EF29467F9D49B8CC60A64B91EF2743873145C7C553026222C125B044E388F1. Full boot/gameplay/release acceptance remain open; whole-project estimate23.87% (rounded24%).

XFB OWNERSHIP SOURCE REVIEW (2026-10-15, READ-ONLY): Traced the wait through src/sysdolphin/baselib/video.c, src/aurora/lib/dolphin/vi/presentation.hpp, src/aurora/lib/gx/xfb.hpp, and the standalone src/pc/video_slots.c prototype. The owner loop waits when no XFB is FREE; copy submission holds a slot through GPU completion, then NEXT/DRAWDONE/display transitions keep the active image unavailable until VI accepts and promotes a replacement. Aurora also pins framebuffers for current/draft/pending presentation tickets. This makes the wait a real lifetime/back-pressure safeguard. Do not bypass it based only on timing numbers. The prototype's separate GPU-complete and presentation-accepted acknowledgements are not wired into production HSD. Next diagnostic: count each slot state and completion/acceptance timestamp while a wait occurs, then design an isolated PC-only change with explicit retirement proof. No source/runtime code changed or rebuilt; 120/240 acceptance remains false.

Status: VERIFIED scoped production renderer fix;overall PARTIALLY VERIFIED.
